claims.text: Introducing a thin, coherent Nb transition layer into CoCrFeMnNi-type HEA multilayers will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces exhibit significant diffusion-mediated creep under high-temperature conditions.
Grain-boundary sliding or Nabarro–Herring creep may mediate the high-temperature creep of these HEA multilayers.
A nanometer-thick Nb layer is to be inserted at the interfaces between HEA layers.
The inserted Nb layer will form a coherent interface.
The Nb layer has a lattice parameter intermediate between those of the adjoining HEA layers.
The intermediate lattice parameter of the Nb layer will reduce interfacial lattice mismatch.
The coherent Nb interface will alter interfacial diffusion pathways.
The Nb interlayer has an intermediate diffusivity relative to the adjoining materials.
The Nb interlayer will lower localized diffusion rates at the interfaces.
Lower interfacial diffusion rates will reduce effective vacancy migration and suppress diffusion-mediated deformation.
The Nb-modified interface will facilitate dislocation nucleation and motion.
Facilitating dislocation nucleation and motion will promote dislocation-mediated creep.
Nb-containing multilayers will show a measurable change, described as a reduction, in creep activation energy relative to the baseline.
Nb-containing multilayers will show increased dislocation activity relative to multilayers without Nb under identical test conditions.
Baseline HEA multilayers without an Nb interlayer are dominated by diffusion-controlled creep at high temperatures.
The proposed transition is expected only when lattice misfit is moderate and the Nb layer remains coherent.
Excessive film thickness or loss of interfacial coherency may prevent the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
The quantitative effect of Nb-layer thickness and the temperature range of the transition are not yet determined.
